Theorem
[Contraction mapping principle]1. ch5:5.1\group chapter-5 Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0086

↗ gt.def5.1.contraction-mapping Every contraction $T$ on a Banach space $\B $ has a unique fixed point.
Proof

Source: gilbarg-trudinger:page-0086

\sketch For $x_m=T^m x_0$, iteration of (1) gives

\[ \| x_n-x_m\| \leq \frac{\theta ^m}{1-\theta }\| Tx_0-x_0\| \qquad (n\geq m). \]

Completeness yields $x_m\to x$, and continuity gives $Tx=x$. Applying (1) to two fixed points proves uniqueness.

□
